rule.description: One consolidated runtime interface (umbrella include + uniform lifecycle phases + shared configuration record) forces translation units and subsystem implementors to depend on declarations and operands of that interface they do not use.

checks.description: Detect subsystem lifecycle handlers that are forced to accept the shared runtime configuration operand of the fat interface without consuming it, which is what the uniform lifecycle signature imposes on phases a subsystem does not own.
checks.detected_relation: subsystem implementor -> unused interface operand of the fat lifecycle
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The interface exceeds the implementor dependency boundary: each subsystem must occupy every lifecycle phase even for phases that do not apply to it, so it carries dependencies (the shared type and its parameter) it never uses. Detected by Clang-Tidy misc-unused-parameters.

checks.description: Detect translation units whose subsystem declarations are obtained through the consolidated runtime interface instead of a focused provider included directly, including dependencies kept alive by compatibility shim headers.
checks.detected_relation: translation unit -> whole fat interface via shim or indirect provider
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The interface exceeds the consumer dependency boundary: to use a single subsystem declaration, a translation unit must depend on the entire consolidated runtime interface. Detected by Clang-Tidy misc-include-cleaner.

excluded.detail: lib/argtable and lib/log headers are external dependencies wrapped by the project, not part of the injected runtime interface; their include relations are outside the rule.
The CUnit test harness includes no project header; it is analyzed for completeness but cannot fuse to the runtime interface.

The registry and the lifecycle drivers implement the fat interface but include the consolidated header directly and consume their operands; the rule detects the forced dependents, not the interface implementation site itself.
